title: Flagger: Cooperative Acceleration for Large-Scale Cross-Silo Federated Learning Aggregation
problem: Cross-silo federated learning using homomorphic encryption (HE) for privacy faces prohibitive computational and communication overhead when scaled: expensive cryptographic computations, inflated ciphertext sizes, excessive network traffic, enormous data volumes, and redundant data movements that overwhelm CPU-centric aggregators.
motivation: Large-scale federated learning requires efficient privacy-preserving aggregation to overcome CPU bottlenecks and enable practical deployment of encrypted model aggregation.
method: Flagger uses specialized hardware accelerators positioned close to where data lives—Data Processing Units (DPUs) in the network and Computational Storage Drives (CSDs) inside storage. These accelerators handle the expensive encryption computations directly at their locations instead of sending encrypted data back to the CPU. Flagger-Runtime software coordinates these accelerators and enables them to exchange data directly with each other, reducing unnecessary data movement through the central processor that was creating bottlenecks.
key_novelty: Flagger distributes encryption computations to specialized accelerators in the network (DPU) and storage (CSD), which coordinate together as a unified system instead of overloading a single CPU.
contributions: Cooperative near-data processing architecture combining DPU and CSD for privacy-preserving federated learning aggregation
Flagger-DPU and Flagger-CSD implementations for in-network and in-storage homomorphic encryption acceleration
Flagger-Runtime software layer enabling NDP coordination and direct peer-to-peer data exchanges
436% average speedup on federated learning aggregation compared to CPU-centric baselines
primary_theme: cooperative near-data processing for encrypted federated learning
